relevance_note: The case report describes one identifiable man with a TNFAIP3 variant ("the patient was diagnosed with HA20") plus four previously published HA20 patients with T1DM listed in Table 2, all with individual-level detail.
method_note: Read the paper, the schema and the rules only. Table 2 is a patients-as-columns table (data columns P1-P5); Table 2's P5 is the same person as the case-report patient of the text: the Reference cell says "This study" and P5's variant c.1467_1468delinsAT p.Q490*, sex Male, age at onset of diabetes 19, anti-GAD 22.39, TG 1.08 and LDL-c 2.32 match the narrative and Table 1. One single individuals row is therefore used, labelled "P5" (the paper's own label for this person in Table 2; the text only ever calls him "the patient"/"our patient", a role word), and the narrative data were merged into it. No cell in this paper contains stacked values separated by " / ", so D-31 did not apply. Contradictions found: (1) Table 2 gives Arthralgia "yes" for P2 and P5, while the text states "these five patients did not present with other clinical manifestations of HA20, including early onset IBD, muscle-skeletal disorders with arthralgia and arthritis, and recurrent fever"; both statements are emitted as phenotypic_features rows and the checklist item "arthritis or arthralgia" is left not reported for P2 and P5. (2) Table 2 gives P5 age at the appearance of initial symptoms "5", while the text says the oral/genital ulcers began "since early childhood"; the narrative wording was used for age_at_onset and the table value is not recorded. (3) The text reports increased thyroid-related antibodies for P5 but Table 2 records Hashimoto thyroiditis "no" for P5; the table cell is used for the checklist item and both findings are recorded separately. Group statements used only where the group is named ("these five patients"): early onset IBD, muscle-skeletal disorders with arthralgia and arthritis, and recurrent fever were marked excluded for P1-P5 with evidence_basis "inferred from group statement"; counts without names ("4/5", "3/5") were not used to exclude anyone. The table's "no" and "Negative" cells are plain words, not undefined symbols. Table 2 P1's "cytopaenias, enteropathy and interstitial lung disease" was recorded as three separate features; "cytopenia (autoimmune)" was marked observed for P1 and this is a judgement on a cell printed under "Other autoinflammatory diseases". CRP for P5 is 5.8 against the table's normal range 0-6, but the paper never calls it normal, so "elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)" was left not reported. age_at_diagnosis for P5 is the stated age at diagnosis of type 1 diabetes (19 years), not an HA20 diagnosis age. publications.n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated were both set to 5, the five patients with HA20 and T1DM the authors summarize; the 117 literature cases and the 60 families they cite elsewhere were not used.

The liver function was improved by using ursodeoxycholic acid 0.75 mg/d during the follow-up.
A new nonsense mutation in TNFAIP3 was identified and the patient was diagnosed with HA20.
We report a novel pathogenic mutation in TNFAIP3 that results in HA20 in a patient with T1DM.
Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome high-throughput sequencing technology
As a result, a c.1467_1468delinsAT heterozygous mutation in the gene TNFAIP3, located in exon 7, was discovered, resulting in a stop-gained type mutation, p.Q490*
